## Historical audit: S0151

**Scope.** This is chunk 1 of 2 of the student trajectory; the other chunk and the referenced images are not visible here. All citations below refer to S0151, original file `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_pilot/results/r1/scene_rsi_pilot/C2/development/commons_118588033/trajectory.jsonl`.

| Evidence | Observation and limit |
|---|---|
| Goal: line 1, `model_request` | Reconstruct an indoor photograph as editable, separate SceneAct geometry, matching viewpoint, objects, colors and occlusion. The student’s interpretation of a ship accommodation compartment is a hypothesis, not independently established scene identity. |
| Initial construction: lines 3–4, student `model_response` and step 1 `execute` | The program constructs multiple owners: architecture, three-tier bunks, equipment, lockers, chair, machine, column, wall fittings, bench and lamps. It groups frame, cushions and other components under owners and specifies approximate support coordinates. These operations do not verify actual contact, connections, pose or visibility. |
| Appearance and camera: lines 3–4 | The program uses colored primitive surfaces, a world, area lights and locally copied lamp materials; no image texture is used in the visible code. Material identity and texture fidelity are unverified. A camera and curved lamp/column approximations are specified, not geometrically validated. |
| First validation and exploration: lines 5–10, `execution_result`, `select`, and student response | Step 1 returned `ok: true` and saved a render; it was selected. The student received the render and reported estimated near/far anchor mismatches, including a low column foot and lockers, then independently proposed a camera-only revision. Those coordinates are student visual estimates, not measurements independently checked here. |
| Camera revision: lines 11–14 | Step 2 executed with the viewpoint advanced and target lowered; `ok: true`, render saved, and step 2 selected. This establishes operability, not that camera pose or framing matched the photograph. |
| Lighting revision: lines 17–21 | The student estimated that step 2 was brighter and flatter than the reference, while reporting excessive cropping and remaining furniture displacement. Step 3 reduced area-light power to 42% and world strength from .32 to .10, retaining the camera; it also copied lamp mesh data before local material edits. Execution returned `ok: true`, saved an image, and step 3 was selected. The predicted visual improvement is not independently verified. |

**Teacher input and adoption.** No teacher event or teacher-specific feedback is visible in this chunk. The student did receive runner results, render images and procedural comparison/scheduling prompts (lines 8 and 15); the subsequent camera and lighting revisions are consistent with those prompts, but do not establish receipt or adoption of any unseen teacher advice.

**Outcome and uncertainty.** Three nonempty programs ran successfully in the visible portion. The last visible selection is step 3; formal final outcome, regression tests, later selection and any interruption are **unknown**, not an established overall success or failure. Images were not supplied to this audit, so multiple-object visibility, actual material appearance, support/collision, part connection, object pose, shadow quality and reference agreement remain unverified. The student’s claimed cropping and brightness discrepancies are unresolved hypotheses.

**Lessons.** Transferable: separate operational success from visual and geometric correctness, and isolate camera and illumination changes when testing hypotheses. Task-specific: the column, lockers and particular lighting reductions are anchors and choices for this reconstruction only; their numerical values should not be generalized.
